title: CLO 2025.0 - Materials
description: This video will introduce updates related to materials. Regarding attachments, you can now decide whether to adhere one point or multiple points based on the attachment type to achieve a more realistic simulation effect. In addition, other feature optimizations can help simplify your workflow.
transcript:
In this video, I will introduce the relevant functions of the material for you.  
In the previous version, we could only attach one point on the component.  
In the 2025 version, we have improved the interaction between the component and the clothing.  
Now we can attach multiple points of the same component to the clothing.  
For complex component styles, we may need to attach two or more points of the component.  
First, we can use the option to move the tool to select the component.  
Then click the quick arrangement button.  
Place the component near the ideal position on the clothing.  
This is a simple placement process and will not produce any adhesion effect.  
In the new version, the tool is combined with the component.  
The operation is similar to fixing the plate to the plate.  
In the new version, the tool is combined with the component.  
The tool is combined with the component.  
Using the tool, we can click the point on the component.  
Then click the point to be attached to the clothing.  
The first group of points is created.  
We can use the same method to attach the second group of points on the component.  
These points will be displayed in dark red and virtual.  
Let's see the result after opening the simulation.  
The two points on the component are perfectly integrated on the clothing.  
If necessary, you can also attach more points on the component.  
If you want to edit the position of the armor, please use the edit armor tool.  
You can edit in 3D and 2D windows.  
Just select the point of the armor and drag its position.  
Open the simulation and check the effect.  
To delete the armor, just select it.  
Then right-click to delete in the menu.  
Or press the delete button.  
Therefore, you can now decide to attach one point or more points according to the component type  
to achieve a more realistic simulation effect.  

In the 2025.0 version,  
you can follow the designated naming method.  
After adding the pattern to the text,  
other PBR stickers are automatically imported.  
First, before importing PBR stickers,  
we need to store all PBR stickers in the same folder.  
Then change the name of the sticker according to the name of the file.  
We need to follow the naming convention for the image, the draft line, and the PBR sticker name—  
these three components make up the image naming rule.  
To ensure that all PBR stickers can be correctly imported,  
the image name should be placed at the beginning.  
The name can be self-defined.  
Each PBR sticker uses the same image name.  
The software can identify that these stickers belong to the same group.  
The draft line is placed behind the image name  
and in the middle of the entire name.  
The PBR sticker name should be placed at the end.  
The name of the PBR sticker also needs to follow the naming rule.  
It will affect the import position of the picture in the clover attribute editor.  
To do this,  
you can use the content shown now  
to name your own PBR stickers.  
You can also refer to the official website for detailed information.  

In the attribute editor,  
let's import the text sticker.  
Click the browse button.  
Find the folder where the PBR stickers are placed.  
Select the text.  
Then click open.  
At this time, you will see a pop-up message  
asking whether to continue.  
Click yes.  
In the attribute editor,  
add the text sticker and other PBR stickers at the same time.  
Click no  
to add only the text sticker.  
Other PBR stickers in the attribute editor  
will not be imported or updated.  
Here we click yes.  
You can see that the text sticker and other PBR stickers  
are added to the corresponding positions.  
You can also import new text stickers  
to replace the existing text stickers in the attribute editor.  
Other related PBR stickers will be added and updated at the same time.  
You can also add other PBR stickers besides fabric  
using this new function.  
For example, stickers,  
self-defined name lines, and so on.  
With this new function,  
you can upload all PBR stickers at once  
and paste the picture.  

The following is about the 2025 version’s  
improvement of the text editor.  
There are two main points.  
One is that you can provide more picture format options.  
Use the format that you need to save the picture.  
The other is support for storing combined layer images.  
Open the text editor.  
We can add more pictures  
and edit these pictures  
to achieve various design effects.  
After editing and adjusting the settings,  
click Save Picture to save the picture result.  
Users can click below the window  
to select the picture format.  
You can export the selected picture to the desired format.  
Now supporting PNG, JPEG, and TIFF file formats.  
Therefore, you can choose the file format according to your needs.  

You can also choose whether to save the combined layer image.  
After selecting the layer images to be saved and combined,  
an additional layer image is added to the combined layer images.  
At the same time, the separated text layer images will be stored normally.  
If you cancel the selection,  
only separate single text layer images are stored according to existing rules.  
This is the same as the default storage result before.  
Here, click OK after setting up.  
Open the storage folder.  
You can see the single layer image and combined image stored.  

By providing multiple image formats and new storage options,  
when users use the text editor to design text,  
it offers more flexibility.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.0 - Materials
chunks.content: ## Multiple Attachment Points for Components in CLO 2025.0 This section explains the enhanced functionality in CLO 2025.0 that allows multiple attachment points of a single component to be linked to clothing, improving simulation realism for complex component styles. In CLO 2025.0, users can attach multiple points of the same component to clothing, unlike previous versions which allowed only one attachment point. This is particularly useful for complex component designs requiring two or more attachment points. ### Procedure for Attaching Multiple Points 1. Use the **Move Tool** to select the component. 2. Click the **Quick Arrangement** button to place the component near the ideal position on the clothing. This step only positions the component without adhesion effects. 3. The tool is now combined with the component, enabling operations similar to fixing one plate to another. 4. Click a point on the component, then click the corresponding point on the clothing to create the first group of attachment points. 5. Repeat the process to attach additional groups of points on the component. These points appear in dark red and as virtual markers. 6. Open the simulation to verify that the multiple points on the component are perfectly integrated with the clothing. 7. Additional points can be added if necessary to refine the attachment. ### Editing and Deleting Attached Armor - Use the **Edit Armor Tool** to modify the position of attached components in both 3D and 2D windows by selecting and dragging armor points. - To delete attached armor, select it, then right-click and choose delete or press the delete key. This feature grants flexibility to attach one or multiple points on a component based on the complexity of the design, enabling more realistic garment simulations. --- ## PBR Sticker Import and Naming Conventions in CLO 2025.0 This section covers the new automated import process for PBR (Physically Based Rendering) stickers in CLO 2025.0 and the required naming conventions to ensure correct grouping and placement. ### PBR Sticker Folder and Naming Rules - Store all related PBR stickers in the same folder before import. - Rename stickers following a specific convention combining three parts: **Image Name**, **Draft Line**, and **PBR Sticker Name**. - The **Image Name** is placed at the beginning of the filename and can be user-defined; it identifies the group of stickers. - The **Draft Line** follows the image name and is positioned in the middle. - The **PBR Sticker Name** is at the end and determines the sticker’s position in the CLO attribute editor. - Adhering to this naming convention allows the software to correctly identify and import related PBR stickers as a set. ### Importing Stickers in the Attribute Editor 1. In the attribute editor, click **Browse** and select the folder containing the PBR stickers. 2. Select the text sticker file and click **Open**. 3. A prompt will appear asking whether to continue importing. - Clicking **Yes** imports the text sticker along with all associated PBR stickers.

chunks.content: - The **PBR Sticker Name** is at the end and determines the sticker’s position in the CLO attribute editor. - Adhering to this naming convention allows the software to correctly identify and import related PBR stickers as a set. ### Importing Stickers in the Attribute Editor 1. In the attribute editor, click **Browse** and select the folder containing the PBR stickers. 2. Select the text sticker file and click **Open**. 3. A prompt will appear asking whether to continue importing. - Clicking **Yes** imports the text sticker along with all associated PBR stickers. - Clicking **No** imports only the selected text sticker without updating others. 4. The stickers are added to their respective positions in the attribute editor. 5. Importing new text stickers will replace existing ones and update related PBR stickers simultaneously. 6. Besides fabric-related stickers, this function supports importing other PBR stickers such as custom lines and decals. 7. This bulk import feature streamlines uploading and pasting multiple PBR stickers at once. Detailed naming guidelines and examples are available on CLO’s official website. --- ## Text Editor Enhancements in CLO 2025.0 This section explains the major improvements to the text editor in CLO 2025.0, focusing on expanded image format support and new options for saving combined layer images. ### Supported Image Formats The text editor now allows exporting images in multiple formats: - **PNG** - **JPEG** - **TIFF** Users can select the preferred format when saving edited pictures, offering flexibility depending on project needs. ### Combined Layer Image Storage - Users can choose to save combined layer images along with separate text layer images. - When enabled, selected text layers are merged into an additional combined image file. - The original individual text layer images are still saved separately. - If this option is disabled, only separate single text layer images are saved, consistent with previous versions. ### Usage 1. Open the text editor and add or edit pictures. 2. After adjustments, click **Save Picture**. 3. Select the desired file format from the options below the window. 4. Choose whether to save combined layers. 5. Confirm by clicking **OK**. 6. The storage folder will contain both the individual layer images and the combined layer image if selected. These enhancements provide users with greater control over text design export, enabling more versatile workflows for graphic and material design in CLO. --- # Summary CLO 2025.0 introduces significant improvements in material handling, including multi-point component attachment for better simulation accuracy, automated and convention-based PBR sticker importing for streamlined workflow, and enhanced text editor capabilities supporting multiple image formats and combined layer storage. These features collectively enhance design flexibility, realism, and efficiency in garment visualization and material editing.
